### Round log (pilot run, SF1 data, old geomean bar)
- E0001/E0002 contains-selectivity 0.04: estimates moved but the SF1 plan did not change, so it was retired. AT SF10 THE PLAN IS DIFFERENT (see below).

- Ask implementers to build in the background and to EXPLAIN-check before the full bench.
- `dbe-tool sql "SET x=..; <q>; <q>"` prints per-statement ms. Good for cheap timing.
- `dbe-tool profile <inst> | grep -E ...` gives the full plan, which is cheaper than reading profile.md (truncated).
- rules.md: never change default settings.
- Planner estimates after LIKE filters and outer joins are off by 5-1000x.
- VERIFY probe/build sides in the plan BEFORE proposing join ideas. The plan changes with scale factor!

issues.title: Contains-filter scan selectivity to flip q09 build sides at SF10
issues.hypothesis: At the new data size (SF10), q09's two most expensive joins have their build side on the larger input. I verified this with `dbe-tool profile q09.m0`, where in HASH_JOIN the right child is the build side. (1) For l_orderkey=o_orderkey, the build is the full orders scan (15M rows) and the probe is lineitem⋈part (3.27M rows); the operator costs 2.97s CPU. (2) For p_partkey=ps_partkey AND l_suppkey=ps_suppkey, the build is partsupp⋈supplier (8M rows) and the probe is the same 3.27M stream; it costs 2.82s CPU. Together these are about 5.8s of q09's roughly 10s CPU. Two things cause this. The part scan filter contains(p_name,'ghost') gets the flat DEFAULT_SELECTIVITY of 0.2, so part is estimated at 400k rows while the actual count is 109k. That makes lineitem⋈part about 12M estimated versus 3.27M actual, which is comparable to orders (15M) and larger than partsupp (8M), so the optimizer builds on orders and partsupp. With selectivity 0.04 the estimate becomes about 2.4M. That is far below both 15M and 8M, so the build-probe optimizer should put the 3.27M side on the build side of both joins. orders (15M) and partsupp (8M) would then become probes and get bloom/min-max filters. E0002 tested exactly this code at SF1 and saw no plan change, because at SF1 orders was already the probe side. The data size has changed the situation since then.
issues.plan: Re-implement E0002's minimal change, restricted to contains(). In src/optimizer/join_order/relation_statistics_helper.cpp, add a file-local static `IsContainsFilter(const TableFilter&)`. It returns true for an ExpressionFilter whose expression is a BoundFunctionExpression named "contains" with a non-empty VARCHAR constant argument. It also recurses into ConjunctionAndFilter children. Look up the actual filter classes in src/planner/filter/ (expression_filter, conjunction_filter) and handle OPTIONAL_FILTER the same way as the surrounding code. Do NOT match prefix(), suffix(), LIKE with a single leading %, NOT, or OR. Suffix patterns like '%BRASS' are genuinely about 0.2 selective. In ExtractGetStats (around line 146-151), when there is no equality filter and a non-optional filter is a contains filter, use 0.2*0.2 instead of DEFAULT_SELECTIVITY. Keep the change out of headers, i.e. file-local constexpr. STEP 1, before the bench: build in the background, then run EXPLAIN ANALYZE on q09.m0 with `dbe-tool sql`. Confirm that the l_orderkey join now has the lineitem/part side as the build (right child) and orders as the probe, and the same for partsupp. If the plan does not flip, look at src/optimizer/build_probe_side_optimizer.cpp to see why (width or cost terms), report that, and stop. STEP 2: run the full bench.
issues.expected_gain: q09 (24% of total time, 1.2s): if both joins flip, the hash table builds go from 15M+8M rows down to 2×3.27M, and orders and partsupp get bloom-filtered probes. Expected 30-50% faster on q09. Other templates are unchanged unless they have a contains filter.
issues.generality: Any query with a '%word%' LIKE or contains() filter on a dimension table that is joined to a fact table. Substring matches are almost always much more selective than 20%. It could get slower when a contains literal is very unselective, such as a single common character, which could flip a join the wrong way. A fallback option is to apply it only for literals of 3 or more characters.
issues.risk: Low-medium. The diff only changes estimates in one file. The main risk is plan changes in hidden templates that use contains filters. E0002 already showed that this code builds and moves the estimates as intended.
